channel.title: Smart Cities Dive - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Smart Cities Dive (smartcitiesdive.com)

item.title: Tampa Bay Rays unveil plans for $2.3B ballpark, mixed-use development
item.description: The Major League Baseball franchise has long sought a new home. Last week it published video renderings that depict a 31,000-seat venue anchoring a “walkable, retail-rich district."

item.title: Where 5 air taxi pilot projects will begin this year
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration’s program to bring advanced air mobility to the skies will also address cargo drones and emergency medical response across 26 states.

item.title: Federal funding at risk as House advances anti-sanctuary bill
item.description: The Shut Down Sanctuary Policies Act would redirect law-enforcement funding to cities and states that cooperate with federal immigration enforcement and would allow crime victims to sue local governments.

item.title: How Durham, North Carolina, kick-started affordable housing development
item.description: A $95 million bond agreement in 2019 has led to a swell of affordable housing units in the city. More local governments are following suit.

item.title: Zoox now testing robotaxis in 10 cities
item.description: The Amazon subsidiary added Dallas and Phoenix and is using “hundreds of test fleet vehicles” to map U.S. cities and validate its software.

item.title: Florida advances bill to bypass local zoning, allow residential development on brownfields
item.description: The Infill Redevelopment Act would increase housing supply in the state’s denser South Florida counties.

item.title: HUD appeals ruling that paused its plans to cut Housing First
item.description: The agency wants to shift away from long-term supportive housing in favor of transitional housing with work requirements and addiction treatment mandates.

item.title: Trump administration unveils new plan for some homeless veterans: legal guardianship
item.description: The Department of Veterans Affairs is teaming up with the Department of Justice for the initiative, which an advocacy group calls dehumanizing.

item.title: The path to building connected communities
item.description: Walkable, bikeable neighborhoods are an economic engine, a public health strategy and a blueprint for building resilient cities. Cities across the U.S. are proving they’re both achievable and scalable.

item.title: Chicago might buy its downtown intercity bus station
item.description: Four bus lines serve the Midwest from the former Greyhound terminal. If the city doesn’t act, bus operators could lose access to the station.
